title: How many children does the average woman in the world have today?
subtitle: Guess the world's births per woman today, take a clue and guess again, then see how it halved since the 1960s, and South Korea's record low.
form: revise (guess on a bar, clue, guess again)
notes: OWID/UN WPP 2024: world 5.31 in 1963 (peak; 1960 was 4.70 because of China's famine, so 1963 is used), 2.25 in 2023; India 1.98, China 1.0; South Korea 5.99 (1960) to 0.72 (2023) - Hong Kong and Macao are as low or lower, so 'one of the lowest anywhere'. Payoff drawn as people: mother with 5 babies vs 2 and a faint third; 10 Korean women over 7 babies with 'steady: 21'. First ask uses reveal:false then revise:g1 (no reference cast used revise before; it rendered fine in frames). Review round: bars 5.3 and 2.3 (rounded, voice 'over five' / 'about two point three'); South Korea drawn as mothers with babies (6 vs a 0.72-faded baby) then 10 women over 21 baby outlines with 7 filled and 'only 1/3'; 'one of the steepest falls', 'among the very lowest'. The revise ask starts from the first guess in the live player (player.ts keeps it as a lighter mark); the frames tool shows the handle's default start instead, and the first guess is not shown during the clue beat (engine). The ask question replaces the heading on a bar guess (engine).
